extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.publisher: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was collected by aggregating samples from numerous existing audio, text, and image datasets across three subsets (Listening, Speaking, Viewing). The collected data then underwent a four-stage curation process involving deduplication, validation, categorization, and sampling.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete or unsuitable instances were excluded during the validation stage.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of audio clips (featuring sounds, music, human speech, and background noise), text instructions and datasets (including role profiles and questions), and a wide variety of images from 30 disciplines and 30 formats (diagrams, tables, photos, etc.) sourced from dozens of existing datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human judges independently evaluated a random 10% sample of model responses across 13 tasks to validate the automated evaluation scheme.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The automated model-based evaluation showed strong agreement with human judgments, with Pearson correlation coefficients ranging from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92) and an overall agreement rate of 96.1%.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b (for content quality assessment), emotion2vec (for emotion probabilities), UTMOS (for speech quality scoring), and Whisper-Large-v3 (for speech transcription).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases stemming from its reliance on academic and synthetic source data. Additionally, the role-play subset relies on a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or exclude certain user personas.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is primarily monolingual (English), which limits its generalization to diverse linguistic settings. It also evaluates models in an offline, static manner, failing to capture real-time deployment factors like latency, continuous listening, or user interruptions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset's inclusion of voice imitation tasks introduces risks of identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. The authors have implemented safeguards to minimize harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset collects and utilizes audio clips of identifiable speakers for voice imitation, as well as specific cultural/demographic roles (e.g., Chinese roles).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating and testing voice assistants. It is explicitly prohibited from being used to train models for the purpose of cheating on the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The maintainers have established a data governance process that includes auditing, removal, and updating of assets in response to consent or licensing issues.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sampling data from categorized problems to balance the ratio of different tasks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text preprocessing for TTS (replacing special tokens, rewriting text, rephrasing options), deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, and validation by excluding incomplete or unsuitable instances.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: we conduct a human evaluation of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B’s outputs (Xu et al., 2025). We randomly sampled 10% of the model’s responses from each of the 13 tasks, resulting in 1050 examples. These responses are then independently evaluated by human judges.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Table 6 shows a very strong agreement between our automated model-based evaluation scheme (using gpt-oss-20b (OpenAI et al., 2025)) and human judgments across various tasks. All reported Pearson correlation coefficients between the model’s scores and human ratings are notably high (ranging from 0.73 to 1.00, with an overall correlation of 0.92)... The overall agreement rate is 96.1%.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: For content quality, we use gpt-oss-20b (OpenAI et al., 2025) to assess response texts with thirteen evaluator prompts... For emotion, we use emotion2vec (Ma et al., 2023) to get the emotion probabilities... To measure speech quality, we employ UTMOS (Saeki et al., 2022)... we first transcribe the speech outputs using Whisper-Large-v3 (Radford et al., 2022)

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Fourth, like many benchmarks, VoiceAssistant-Eval may carry biases from its source data and design choices. The questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources... For example, the role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts. These roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Although we include five Chinese roles in the role-play task, all other prompts and evaluations are in English. This monolingual focus may not capture the full variability of real user interactions... VoiceAssistant-Eval evaluates models in an offline, static manner, which might not capture certain practical deployment factors.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: To mitigate misuse risks (e.g., identity spoofing, harassment, fraud), we (i) prohibit training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent... These measures aim to enable research on personalization while minimizing harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The VoiceAssistant-Eval dataset is not supposed to be used, though the risk exists, for training models for cheating. We intend for researchers to use this dataset to better evaluate voice assistants and, consequently, facilitate future studies in this area.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
